agreement::drift:buildEvidencePacks.why: SAFE as agreement, DEFECT as duplication. timeline/timeline-enrich.js builds evidence packs for CHARACTERS and timeline/timeline-locations-enrich.js for LOCATIONS; the shared scaffolding is what trips the heuristic. The two are not answering one question. They are, however, the same function specialised by copy rather than by parameter, so the character path and the location path will drift apart under maintenance. Owner: timeline consolidation (teamA-01).

agreement::drift:charactersFromScript.why: DEFECT, small and cheap. casting/lib-castdesk.js and wardrobe/lib-ward.js compute character lines identically — the bodies differ in exactly one line — but return DIFFERENT SHAPES for the same field name: casting returns {scenes: <count>, sceneList: [..]}, wardrobe returns {scenes: [..]}. `scenes` is a number in one module and an array in the other. Anything that ever consumes both gets a length where it expected a list, with no error. Owner: the dedup half of wave 1.1 / finding 9 (the correct implementation already exists elsewhere) — one implementation, one shape.

agreement::drift:cleanLocName.why: DEFECT, low severity, verified by reading all three. timeline/timeline-locations-enrich.js strips a leading 'on ' from a location name; timeline/timeline-locations.js and timeline/timeline.js do not. 'on Sparks Street' therefore normalises to two different canonical names depending on which path reached it, and the same location appears twice on the location list and the DOOD. Owner: the timeline consolidation (teamA-01 backlog); the timeline.js copy should delegate the way countCueLines already does.

agreement::drift:countCueLines.why: DEFECT-IN-WAITING, listed rather than dismissed. timeline/timeline.js delegates to SBParser.countCueLines when it exists and otherwise runs a byte-identical inline copy of timeline/parser.js's regex. Today the two agree. The fallback is the hazard: parser.js is under active edit, and the moment its regex changes, the fallback path keeps the old behaviour with nothing to notice — a copy that is correct only for as long as nobody touches the original. Owner: timeline consolidation; delete the fallback and let a missing SBParser fail loudly.

agreement::drift:csvCell.why: SAFE on the injection question, DEFECT as duplication. Both variants carry the identical guard /^[=+\-@\t\r]/ and prefix an apostrophe, which is the repo rule and the whole point of finding 26; they differ only in unconditional versus conditional quoting, and both are valid CSV for the same input. So there is no live CSV-injection hole in these four files. Keeping the count is what makes this safe to accept: a fifth copy WITHOUT the guard raises the count and fails the gate, which is the outcome finding 26 actually needs. Owner as duplication: shared-helper wave.

agreement::drift:dl.why: SAFE, same class as drift:init. Four Blob-and-anchor download helpers, each with its own filename and mime conventions. UNSURE at the margin: these are the functions that decide what leaves the building, and finding 33 says nothing gates that today. If a rights gate is added it must be added to all four, and this entry should be re-read at that point rather than migrated.

agreement::drift:enrichViaAgent.why: SAFE as agreement, DEFECT as duplication — same two files and same reasoning as drift:buildEvidencePacks: one agent call specialised for characters, one for locations.

agreement::drift:esc.why: SAFE on the question that matters, DEFECT as duplication. All eight variants across all twenty files escape the identical character class & < > " ' to the identical entities; I read boards/boards.js, js/safe-url.js, producer/budget-sheet.js and timeline/timeline-characters.js and diffed the rest by their normalised bodies. The eight 'versions' are null-handling and chained-replace-vs-table style, not coverage. One real difference: the String(s || '') variants render a literal 0 or false as an empty cell, which is a display bug and not an escaping hole. Nothing here is an XSS gap; scripts/scan_html_sinks.mjs is the check that would find one, and it is a separate gate. Owner as duplication: the shared-helper wave (finding 43's quantified-duplication note — esc appears in 38 files). Held at 8 versions: a ninth means somebody wrote a new escaper, which is the event worth failing on.

agreement::drift:getClipLocationRaw.why: DEFECT, same pair and same path as drift:parseLocFromText — timeline/timeline-locations.js and timeline/timeline.js each read a clip's location field. Owner: timeline consolidation.

agreement::drift:inferCastRole.why: DEFECT. timeline/timeline-characters.js and timeline/timeline.js each infer whether a character is a lead, supporting or background from the clips they appear in. Cast role drives the DOOD and therefore what the production is billed for (finding 39), so two answers here are not cosmetic. Owner: timeline consolidation, and it should end up calling js/mastery-resolver.js, which already ranks roles and which no suite currently loads (see coverage::js/mastery-resolver.js).

agreement::drift:init.why: SAFE, and the clearest false-positive class in this check. Nine page bootstraps named init(), each wiring its own page's DOM to its own store. They exceed the 0.55 token-overlap threshold because they share the repo's house idiom ($, addEventListener, readLS, render, toast) — the vocabulary is duplicated, the concept is not, and there is no single correct init() for two of them to disagree about. I did NOT raise the threshold to make this disappear: doing so would weaken the check for the real drift it does catch (parseSceneNums, cleanLocName), and a named entry with a count is the honest way to hold it.

agreement::drift:load.why: SAFE, same class as drift:init. Seven per-module readLS wrappers, each over its own SB_ key with its own default. Shared idiom, not shared concept. Held at seven copies so an eighth is read by a human.

agreement::drift:nameInBlob.why: DEFECT, low severity. timeline/parser.js and timeline/timeline-continuity.js each decide whether a character name occurs in a text blob. Two answers to one question, and continuity conclusions are cited against parser output. Owner: timeline consolidation. parser.js is under edit right now, so re-derive before acting.

agreement::drift:parseHeading.why: DEFECT. timeline/timeline-continuity.js and timeline/timeline-locations.js each parse a scene heading into its parts. This is finding 1 (five modules parse scene numbers differently) inside one module directory. Owner: wave 1.1 — both should call js/lib-scenes.js.

agreement::drift:parseLocFromText.why: DEFECT. timeline/timeline-locations.js and timeline/timeline.js each extract a location from free text, and their results feed the same location list that cleanLocName then normalises differently again (see drift:cleanLocName). Owner: timeline consolidation.

agreement::drift:parseSceneNums.why: DEFECT, and not cosmetic. js/lib-scenes.js parseSceneNums returns STRINGS and accepts A-scenes both ways round (12A and A12); wardrobe/lib-ward.js returns NUMBERS and its token test is /^\d+$/, so it silently DROPS every A-scene. A wardrobe continuity entry tagged '12A' resolves to no scene at all, and even where both match, one side's '12' will never === the other side's 12 in a join. Owner: wave 1.1 (retire the copies onto js/lib-scenes.js). This is the clearest single instance of why finding 49 matters.

agreement::drift:redo.why: SAFE, the mirror of drift:undo: editor/cut-ui.js and timeline/timeline.js each pop from their own redo stack over their own document model. Two editors, two independent histories, nothing shared for them to answer differently.

agreement::drift:removeRow.why: SAFE. distribution removes from {windows, screeners}; finance removes from {pos, petty}. Identical delete-and-compare-lengths idiom over different collections. This is one of the 4/8 modules finding 43 counts as repeating the delete idiom verbatim — a dedup item, not a defect.

agreement::drift:repairAllCharacterDescr.why: DEFECT, listed for the reviewer's attention. The name is character-specific, yet it exists in both timeline/timeline-enrich.js and timeline/timeline.js — that is a genuine second copy of one concept, not a domain split like buildEvidencePacks. Whichever the page calls wins and the other is dead or, worse, is called on a different path with different behaviour. Owner: timeline consolidation (teamA-01). UNSURE: I did not establish which of the two the live page actually reaches; a reviewer should.

agreement::drift:save.why: SAFE, same class as drift:init (a shared house idiom, not a shared concept). Nine per-module localStorage writers over nine different SB_ keys, each serialising its own module's state shape. There is no single correct save() two of them could disagree about. Held at nine copies so a tenth is read by a human.

agreement::drift:searchLink.why: SAFE. festivals, locations and props each build a Google search URL, and the three bodies differ only in the query they compose for their own domain — festival deadlines, a scouted location, a props house. There is no shared concept for them to disagree about; they share an idiom, which is what the token-overlap heuristic measures. All three satisfy the repo's rule that an unverified entry gets a search link rather than an invented phone or URL. Worth collapsing to one helper eventually, not a correctness risk.

agreement::drift:setBudget.why: SAFE as agreement, listed as a dedup item. producer/incentives.js and producer/sales-forecast.js each store a budget figure into their own panel state; they are two setters on two views, not two answers to one question. UNSURE at the margin: if a later wave makes one of them the canonical budget entry point, the other becomes a second writer of the same number and this must be re-read rather than migrated forward.

agreement::drift:setStatus.why: SAFE. contracts (draft/sent/signed on a deal), music (cue statuses) and screening (open/done on a note) each validate against their own vocabulary and mutate their own store. Same three-line idiom, three unrelated state machines — nothing one could get 'wrong' relative to another. Coincidental name that the heuristic cannot separate from real drift, correctly reported and correctly accepted.

agreement::drift:toast.why: SAFE, same class as drift:init. Six copies of the same six-line toast, each addressing its own page's toast element by id. Pure boilerplate duplication for the shared-helper wave.

agreement::drift:undo.why: SAFE. editor/cut-ui.js and timeline/timeline.js each maintain their own undo stack over their own document model. Two editors, two histories; nothing shared to disagree about.

agreement::drift:wire.why: SAFE, same class as drift:init. Four event-binding routines, each attaching its own page's handlers to its own page's elements; they overlap on addEventListener and the $ helper and on nothing else. Held at four copies.

agreement::splitScenes:answers.why: DEFECT, the highest-consequence entry on this list. Nine runnable splitScenes implementations give two answers for one script carrying a FADE IN: preamble and an A-scene, and NEITHER answer is right: eight modules return 4 scenes with an empty first scene number (they count the preamble as a scene and discard the printed number), timeline/timeline-budget.js returns 3 with a null number. The fixture has three real scenes, 1 / 1A / 2. Every downstream number a producer reads — page count, eighths, the props breakdown, the risk assessment, the DOOD — is quoted against these. Root cause is finding 17, the non-capturing group in timeline/parser.js that throws the printed number away. Owner: wave 1.1 (one scene model, js/lib-scenes.js + SB_Scenes_v1, retire the copies). timeline/parser.js is under edit by another agent as this is written, so this entry may change shape before it clears; it must clear, not be re-listed.

api-reach::boards/lib-shots.js.why: SAFE. blank() returns the module's empty store literal and is reached by every test in the suite that constructs a store, just never named. Same shape as api-reach::investors/lib-invest.js: a constructor helper exercised through its callers. If it ever gains a default that matters (a version stamp, a seeded row), that is a shape a reader depends on and it needs naming.

api-reach::casting/lib-castdesk.js.why: SAFE. uid() mints a random row id. It is unnamed by the suite because there is nothing to assert about a random string beyond uniqueness, and every add path in the suite goes through it. Finding 43's duplication note counts five modules minting their own uid(); collapsing them is a dedup item, not a correctness one.

api-reach::clearance/lib-clear.js.why: DEFECT, and on the E&O path. appearanceRelease and materialsRequest are unnamed by any suite. Finding 20 says 'E&O-ready' can be reached having cleared nothing; these two are the document generators that are supposed to make it mean something. Owner: wave 2.5.

api-reach::contracts/lib-deal.js.why: DEFECT. acctFor, otPct, removeDeal and scaleStatus are unnamed by any suite. acctFor is the crew-to-3000 / cast-to-2000 fix finding 22 calls for and it is untested; scaleStatus is the function finding 42 says prints '(scale)' for half of scale because of a <=. Note this file's round trip only runs at all because I fixed the harness to resolve a CALL-TIME dependency (contracts/lib-deal.js asks for CMoneyMath when a deal is valued, not when it loads) — before that fix the SB_Crew_v1 round trip was skipped entirely and read as one line rather than as a check that did not run. Owner: wave 1.4 / wave 1.5.

api-reach::finance/lib-money.js.why: DEFECT. budgetByAcct and postAcct are never named by any suite that loads finance/lib-money.js — the two functions that decide which account a cost lands on, in the module finding 10 says gets the chart of accounts wrong in at least four places. Owner: wave 1.4.

api-reach::investors/lib-invest.js.why: SAFE. r2 is a two-decimal rounding helper, and the suite that loads investors/lib-invest.js reaches every function that USES it — so the behaviour is exercised on every assertion in that suite, it is simply never named directly. This check is deliberately generous (naming the identifier counts), so an unnamed private-in-spirit helper reached through its callers is the one shape where a violation is a true statement and not a gap. UNSURE at the margin: finding 42 is about rounding, so if wave 1.5 introduces roundHalfAway then r2 should be DELETED in favour of it rather than tested — which would clear this key by removal.

api-reach::js/learn.js.why: DEFECT, minor. cleanCached is unnamed by any suite that loads js/learn.js. The rest of the module is reached. Owner: Phase 4, which replaces this layer wholesale (finding 44) — listed so it is retired deliberately rather than forgotten.

api-reach::js/lib-money-accounts.js.why: DEFECT. 4 of 7 exports unnamed: exists, forDept, isLabor, rollup. This is the shared chart of accounts wave 1.4 introduces to fix four wrong postings (findings 6/10/22). exists() is the guard that would have caught casting/index.html posting to account 1400, which does not exist. Owner: wave 1.4; under active edit.

api-reach::js/lib-money-math.js.why: DEFECT. 9 of 16 exports unnamed by any suite: add, csvNum, csvWhole, dollars, mul, mulCents, pctOfCents, roundHalfAway, sumCents. roundHalfAway and pctOfCents are the explicit-rounding primitives wave 1.5 exists to introduce, and csvNum/csvWhole are the ones that decide whether a raw float reaches a CSV — finding 42's third defect. The decimal money helper being untested is the same failure as having no decimal money helper. Owner: wave 1.5; under active edit.

api-reach::js/lib-money-sheet.js.why: DEFECT, the largest single gap in this check. 13 of 15 exported functions are never named by any suite that loads the file — actualCents, actualTotal, byAcct, byAcctCents, catCents, catTotals, itemActual, itemActualCents, itemEstCents, itemNeedsSync, laborBaseCents, subtotalCents, syncEst. This is the budget sheet's arithmetic, on the SB_BudgetSheet_v1 store that finding 31 says eight modules read, and finding 2 says four of five budget-total implementations are wrong. A module can be loaded and still be untested; that is what mode 5 means one level down. Owner: wave 1.3 (one budget total) / wave 1.5, and the money-suites agent is in this file now — expect movement.

api-reach::js/lib-scenes.js.why: DEFECT, and it is the real one behind ten look-alikes. eighthsOf, normNum and sortScenes are never named by any suite. eighthsOf is the page-eighths measure finding 18 says is 4.4x wrong and which drives both the schedule and the budget; normNum is the A-scene normaliser that drift:parseSceneNums shows two modules disagree about. Until my harness fix this same gap was ALSO charged against ten other modules that merely load lib-scenes.js and do not define these functions, which pointed every reader at the wrong file. Owner: wave 1.1 — the new scene model must not ship with its measure untested.

api-reach::post/lib-post.js.why: DEFECT, low severity but on a live path. parseISO and fmtISO are unnamed by any suite that loads post/lib-post.js. They are the date pair underneath CPost.schedule(), which finding 38 / wave 3 item 3 says is an already-tested business-day dependency scheduler that should be wired up as the prep/wrap calendar. Wiring it up on an untested date parser is how an off-by-one day reaches a call sheet. Owner: wave 3 item 3.

api-reach::production/lib-cast.js.why: SAFE, with a caveat. wikidataDirectorQuery builds a SPARQL query string against Wikidata; it is a query builder, not a decision, and every value it produces is presented to the owner as a link to verify rather than as a fact — which is the repo's rule for unverified data. A test would pin a string literal and assert nothing about correctness. CAVEAT: if a later wave ever consumes the RESULT of that query as data rather than as a suggestion, this stops being safe and must be re-read.

api-reach::projects/lib-vault.js.why: DEFECT, and it is the export boundary. allKeys and isPortable are unnamed by any suite. isPortable is the predicate that decides what may leave the project — finding 33 says nothing gates what leaves the building and finding 34 says continuity photos leave the project. The gate predicate is untested. Owner: wave 2.5 / wave 3 item 2 (rights gate).

api-reach::props/lib-props.js.why: DEFECT, real and specific. dimsFor, fitsThrough and toSetItem are unnamed by any suite. fitsThrough is the check that a prop physically fits through a doorway — a wrong answer there is a truck that arrives and a piece that does not go in the room, which is a shoot day. Owner: the props slice / wave 2.1's sets work, since toSetItem is the props-to-sets handoff.

api-reach::screening/lib-screen.js.why: DEFECT, low severity. removeNote, removeSession and sortNotes are unnamed by any suite. Two deletes and a sort over a local store; nothing downstream reads a number from them. Listed rather than dismissed because removeSession deletes a screening record and a delete with no test is how data disappears quietly. Owner: the screening slice.

api-reach::timeline/timeline-doc.js.why: DEFECT. analyzeDoc and estimateDoc are 2 of this module's 3 exports and neither is named by any suite — the module is effectively loaded and not tested at all, and estimateDoc is a budget estimate. Owner: wave 1.3 / the timeline consolidation. UNSURE: I did not establish whether either is still reachable from a live page; if they are dead they should be deleted, not tested, and finding 12 (green tests over dead features) says deciding which is the actual work.

api-reach::tools/lib-script.js.why: DEFECT. msToTc, tcToMs and revHex are unnamed by any suite. The timecode pair is the same arithmetic that is provably wrong in timeline/timeline-export.js ftc() (see coverage::timeline/timeline-export.js); whether these two agree with it, or with each other round-tripping ms -> tc -> ms, is asserted nowhere. Owner: wave 2.4.

api-reach::tools/lib-sun.js.why: DEFECT. fmtLocal and wmoLabel are unnamed by any suite. fmtLocal is the local-time formatter, and findings 24/28 confirm the timezone bug three times over — the location's utc_offset_seconds is fetched and discarded. The formatter at the centre of a thrice-confirmed timezone defect is untested. Owner: wave 2.2.

api-reach::wardrobe/lib-ward.js.why: DEFECT, small. uniqScenes is unnamed by any suite — and it is the function wardrobe/lib-ward.js parseSceneNums returns THROUGH, i.e. the last step of the A-scene-dropping path in agreement::drift:parseSceneNums. Testing it directly with '12, 12A, 12' would have shown the drop immediately. Owner: wave 1.1.

coverage::boards/boards.js.why: DEFECT, mitigated. 430 lines, 9 document. references; the pure logic it renders lives in boards/lib-shots.js, which IS covered. What is left untested is the page controller. Owner: the boards slice, via a browser harness. Accepted for now on the basis that the numbers a production reads come from the tested lib and not from here.

coverage::editor/timeline-engine.js.why: DEFECT with a mitigating reason. 611 lines, 21 document. references — this is the NLE surface and needs a browser harness, not a node suite. The mitigation is real and the size is why it is still a defect: it is the second-largest unexecuted file in the repo. Owner: wave 2.4. scripts/test_cut.mjs already covers the pure cut logic; the engine itself has nothing.

coverage::js/config.js.why: DEFECT, small but security-adjacent. 103 lines, no document. reference, no suite. It is the single source of truth for the Firebase web config and owner metadata for app.html, workflow/ and editor/. The public apiKey is public by design, but the OWNER LIST is here, and nothing asserts that the five owner ids are what the gate expects or that no secret has been added beside them. A contract test over this file is a dozen lines. Owner: the auth/gate slice (scripts/test_gate.mjs and scripts/test_auth_hardening.mjs already exist and are the natural home).

coverage::js/effects.js.why: SAFE, with the narrowest reason on this list. 503 lines, 11 document. references, and every entry point is documented and written as a silent no-op when its element or browser API is missing — starfield, reveal, typewriter, ticker. It is presentation with no data path: nothing here produces a number a production relies on, and a failure is visible as a missing animation rather than as a wrong figure. This is the one coverage entry I would defend as acceptable indefinitely rather than as owned work. A smoke check that the page still loads with it is already covered by scripts/smoke_pages.mjs.

coverage::js/ffmpeg-wasm.js.why: DEFECT, partially mitigable. 265 lines, no document. reference, no suite. Most of it cannot be executed outside a cross-origin-isolated browser with WASM, which is a real reason no node suite loads it — but assertIsolated() and the blob-worker construction are ordinary logic and are the part most likely to be silently wrong, and neither is exercised even by a browser harness. Owner: the editor/post slice. Accepting the WASM half is defensible; accepting the whole file is what let finding 36 happen.

coverage::js/mastery-resolver.js.why: DEFECT, and the closest thing on this list to a repeat of finding 36. 358 shipped lines, DOM-free, node-evaluable today, and no suite loads it — it is the unified per-shot character/location reference resolver with its own role ranking, i.e. exactly the logic timeline/timeline-characters.js re-infers by hand in drift:inferCastRole. A pure-logic file with no test is the js/budget-engine.js shape, and that one was 1,082 lines wrong by 4.5x. Owner: wave 1.6 for the requirement; whichever Phase 2 team owns the mastery layer for the suite. Cheapest real win on this list.

coverage::js/model-config.js.why: DEFECT with a mitigating reason. 460 lines, 40 document. references — it builds the settings dropdowns — so it needs a browser harness rather than a node suite, and the browser harnesses exist (test_set3d_browser.mjs is the pattern). What is untested is not only the DOM: the PHOTO_MODELS/VIDEO_MODELS capability tables gate which resolutions and aspect ratios a model will accept, and a wrong entry there fails at the API, in front of the owner, with no test between. Owner: the generation/model slice.

coverage::production/production.js.why: DEFECT, mitigated the same way as boards/boards.js — 553 lines of page controller over production/lib-prod.js, which is covered. Not fully safe: production.js:220 is where the DPR's stores are assembled from localStorage, and the SB_TakeLog_v1 mismatch above is exactly a wiring bug in that assembly, which is the layer no test touches. Owner: wave 2.3.

coverage::timeline/pro-cut.js.why: DEFECT with a partial excuse. 228 lines, only 2 document. references, and the clip analysis is genuinely browser-bound (it samples video frames onto a canvas). But the EDL construction and the clamp/threshold arithmetic around it are pure and are what a professional round trip depends on. Owner: wave 2.4 / the editor slice — test the EDL half in node, leave the frame sampling to a browser harness.

coverage::timeline/timeline-characters.j.why: DEFECT. 518 lines, ZERO document. references — pure logic, node-evaluable, no suite. It owns inferCastRole (which the DOOD and therefore cast billing depend on, finding 39) and its own esc/parse copies. There is no browser-only excuse for this one. Owner: timeline consolidation (teamA-01) plus wave 1.6's enumeration requirement.

coverage::timeline/timeline-continuity.j.why: DEFECT. 393 lines, zero document. references, no suite. Owns parseHeading and nameInBlob — two of the drift keys above — so the module that has drifted is also the module nothing runs. Owner: timeline consolidation.

coverage::timeline/timeline-enrich.js.why: DEFECT. 206 lines, zero document. references, no suite. Owns buildEvidencePacks, enrichViaAgent and repairAllCharacterDescriptions. Owner: timeline consolidation.

coverage::timeline/timeline-locations-en.why: DEFECT. 348 lines, zero document. references, no suite. It is the copy of cleanLocName that strips 'on ' where the other two do not, so the untested file is the one that diverges. Owner: timeline consolidation.

coverage::timeline/timeline-locations.js.why: DEFECT. 259 lines, zero document. references, no suite. Owns cleanLocName, parseLocFromText, parseHeading and getClipLocationRaw — four drift keys in one untested file. Owner: timeline consolidation.

coverage::tools/sched-weather.js.why: DEFECT. 161 lines, 5 document. references, no suite. It computes shoot-day dates, sunrise/sunset, golden hours and a risk score off tools/lib-sun.js and a live Open-Meteo call. Findings 14/24/28 say the sun and timezone maths is wrong in two different places and that the fix data (utc_offset_seconds) is already fetched and discarded — and this is one of the consumers, untested. Owner: wave 2.2 (sun and time).

coverage::tools/tools-media-ui.js.why: DEFECT. 516 lines, 17 document. references, no suite — and it is the writer of SB_TakeLog_v1, the store whose three-field mismatch is the first three entries on this list. Owner: wave 2.3, with wave 1.6's enumeration requirement.

coverage::tools/tools-money-ui.js.why: DEFECT. 208 lines, only 1 document. reference, so most of it is node-reachable logic on the money path — the slice PHASE1-SYNTHESIS says is wrong in three independent ways (finding 42). Money code with no test is the least defensible category on this list. Owner: wave 1.5 (money arithmetic). Another agent is editing the money suites as this is written; expect this to clear.

coverage::tools/tools-registers.js.why: DEFECT, and higher-value than its 178 lines suggest. Only 2 document. references, and it is the WRITER for SB_Festivals_v1 and several other registers — every writer shape CHECK 1 derives comes from files like this one. The one module that defines what a stored row looks like is executed by no suite, so a field renamed here silently breaks every reader and the round-trip check would still be comparing the reader against the new shape. Owner: wave 1.6.

coverage::tools/tools-script-ui.js.why: DEFECT. 263 lines, 4 document. references, no suite; it is the script tool's controller and carries its own dl() copy. Owner: wave 1.1's tools consumer, and the pre-cut split of scripts/test_tools.mjs into per-lib suites that PROGRAM.md already schedules for Gate-0 R3b is the natural place to add it.

coverage::workflow/advisor-ui.js.why: DEFECT, and not a mitigated one. 166 lines, 5 document. references, no suite — and this is the file that prints js/learn.js's budgetSummary() to the owner as 'Self-learning' (finding 44), a number that goes UP as the system gets MORE wrong. The untested file is the one presenting the misleading label. PROGRAM.md assigns advisor-ui.js to Phase 4. Owner: Phase 4 (the learning layer replacement), which must not ship without a test that pins what this string claims.

coverage::writer/writer.js.why: DEFECT, mitigated. 232 lines, 5 document. references, page controller; scripts/test_writer.mjs covers the writer logic. Owner: the development slice (wave 3 item 1 territory / finding 19, which is rewriting this area anyway).

inputs::cents:scripts/test_csv_injection.why: DEFECT against a standing rule. PROGRAM.md's standing rules say money fixtures use cents; this suite executes six money modules including js/lib-money-math.js and js/lib-money-sheet.js and every amount in it is a round number, so the rounding behaviour finding 42 is about is never exercised. It is a CSV-injection suite, so the money modules are incidental — but a raw float reaching a CSV cell IS one of finding 42's three defects, which makes cents relevant here rather than noise. Owner: the money-suites agent working now (Gate-0 R1). Expected to clear this wave.

inputs::cents:scripts/test_festivals.mjs.why: DEFECT, same standing rule. festivals/lib-fest.js sums submission fees; every fee in the fixture is round, so feesTotal is never asked to add 65.50 to 41.25. Festival fees in the real world are almost never whole dollars, which makes this the input class the bug would live in. Owner: the festivals slice.

inputs::cents:scripts/test_gate.mjs.why: NOT a money suite. test_gate.mjs is the authentication suite — forged HMACs, expired tokens, cookie shadowing, traversal — and it touches no amount of money at all. It appears here only because this run corrected EXEC_MARK to recognise require()/createRequire as execution, which it had never counted; test_gate transitively loads js/learn.js and is now, correctly, filed as executing it. The cents rule is right for a suite that ASSERTS on money and wrong for one that merely loads a module which happens to handle it. Adding cents fixtures here would test nothing and obscure what the suite is for. The real cents coverage for js/learn.js lives in test_walkforward.mjs and test_ops_money.mjs. Re-examine if test_gate ever asserts on an amount.

roundtrip::uncovered-stores.why: DEFECT, aggregated by design, and the single number on this list most worth watching. 56 SB_* stores have no round-trip case at all, so mode 1 (a fixture inventing a shape no writer produces) is still possible in every one of them; the four that ARE covered found five real mismatches between them, which is the argument for the rest. The count is the ceiling: adding a store without a reader case pushes it up and fails the gate, and every reader case a later wave adds lowers it. RAISED 53 -> 56 by Phase 2 wave 1, which added exactly three stores, verified by diffing the store set against the green tree at cd96f33: SB_ShootDays_v1 (T6, the shoot-day join key), SB_StoryDays_v1 (T10) and SB_PostActuals_v1 (T9). Each is a genuine new store, not a re-listing, and each needs a READERS entry in scripts/test_assurance.mjs — a file NO build team owns, which is why three teams could add a store and none could cover it. That ownership gap is the thing to fix, not the number: give the harness's READERS list an owner, or let each team add its own reader case. For SB_ShootDays_v1 the case is three lines (CShootDays.byDate/indexForDate over a record built by CShootDays.build) and js/lib-shootdays.js is otherwise fully covered by scripts/test_shootdays.mjs. Do NOT migrate this key downward casually - a fall in the count that is not matched by a new READERS entry means a store was DELETED, not covered.
